findings.title: Any span carrying a generic `span.type` attribute now passes the default export filter.
findings.body:
`span.type` is not specific to Claude Code. Other instrumentation sets it too: Datadog/ddtrace bridges, for example, tag spans with `span.type` = `web`, `http`, `sql`, `redis`. With this check, every such span counts as an LLM span, so the default smart filter exports HTTP and DB spans it used to drop. That adds noise and volume to Latitude traces.

Fix: match only on the value, e.g. `key === "span.type"` with an attribute value of `interaction` or `llm_request`. Or rely on the Claude Code-specific keys (`user_prompt`, `llm_request.context`).

findings.title: Model sanitization doesn't handle the `[1m]` suffix shown in the linked issue.
findings.body:
The issue shows Claude Code sending `model: "claude-opus-4-6[1m]"`, with a closing `]` and no ESC byte. `ANSI_SGR_RE` needs `\x1b`. The fallback `/\[[0-9;]*m$/` needs the string to end in `m`. Neither matches, so `gen_ai.request.model` stays `claude-opus-4-6[1m]` and model/pricing lookups for these spans can fail.

The test passes only because it uses a made-up `"claude-opus-4-6\u001b[1m"` instead of the real value.

Fix: also strip a trailing `\[[0-9;]*m\]` (for example `/\[[0-9;]*m\]?$/`). Add a test case with the exact string from the issue.
